notes:
Here are my verse-by-verse notes on Numbers 26:23–43, drawn from the sources available.

---

## Numbers 26:23–43 — Verse-by-Verse Commentary Notes

### Overview of the Chapter

The second census (cf. Numbers 1) is taken on the plains of Moab, after the plague, as the old generation has died out (v. 64–65). Its purposes: (1) to muster Israel for the coming conquest of Canaan, and (2) to prepare for the fair division of the land among the tribes (v. 52–56). The total number counted is 601,730 — a decrease of only 1,820 from the first census, despite 38 years of wilderness wandering. (Enduring Word, https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/; Keil & Delitzsch, https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)

---

### vv. 23–25 — The Tribe of Issachar

**v. 23:** "These were the descendants of Issachar by their clans: The Tolaite clan from Tola, the Punite clan from Puvah…"

- **Gill** notes that the tribe of Issachar was numbered next to Judah because it was encamped under Judah's standard (the east side). He observes that two names differ slightly from the Genesis 46:13 list: "Phuvah" appears as "Pua" and "Job" as "Jashub." (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/numbers/26.htm)
- **Keil & Delitzsch** explain that "Job" (Genesis 46:13) and "Jashub" have the same meaning: both derive from a root signifying "to return." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)
- **The Cambridge Bible** notes the same correspondence with Genesis 46:13 and 1 Chronicles 7:1, confirming the two names carry identical meaning. (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/numbers/26.htm)

**v. 25:** "These were the clans of Issachar, and their registration numbered 64,300."

- **Enduring Word (David Guzik)** records that in the first census Issachar numbered 54,400 (Num. 1:29). Now they are 64,300 — a gain of 9,900 (an 18% increase), suggesting God's blessing on the tribe. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)
- **Precept Austin** likewise notes the increase of 9,900 and cites Allen (EBC) that Issachar held fifth rank in both census lists. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/numbers-26-commentary)
- **Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary** confirms the same numbers: 64,300 in the second census, an increase of 9,900 from 54,400. It notes the "Job"/"Jashub" variation as referring to the same person. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/numbers-26.html)

---

### vv. 26–27 — The Tribe of Zebulun

**v. 26:** "These were the descendants of Zebulun by their clans: The Seredite clan from Sered, the Elonite clan from Elon, and the Jahleelite clan from Jahleel."

- **Keil & Delitzsch** state simply: "The families of Zebulun correspond to the sons named in Genesis 46:14." No variation exists. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)
- **Gill** remarks that Zebulun was numbered next to Issachar, also under Judah's standard. The tribe had three families. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)
- **Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary** notes that the listing here is the same as in Genesis 46:14. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/numbers-26.html)

**v. 27:** "These were the clans of Zebulun, and their registration numbered 60,500."

- **Enduring Word**: Zebulun increased from 57,400 (Num. 1:31) to 60,500 — a gain of 3,100 (about 5%). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)
- **Precept Austin** adds that, unlike other tribes, the further history of Zebulun is not recorded in 1 Chronicles 2–8, calling this "a strange omission." (https://www.preceptaustin.org/numbers-26-commentary)
- **Gill** concurs: "this tribe was increased 3100." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)

---

### v. 28 — The Descendants of Joseph (Introduction)

**v. 28:** "The descendants of Joseph included the clans of Manasseh and Ephraim."

- **Keil & Delitzsch** explain that Joseph's descendants were classified into two leading families according to his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim, who were born before Israel moved to Egypt and were raised to the status of tribe-founders because Jacob adopted them as his own sons (Genesis 48). (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)
- **Gill** observes that Manasseh is mentioned first here, though Ephraim was preferred by Jacob and held the standard. Gill suggests this is because Manasseh now had the greater increase. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)

---

### vv. 29–34 — The Tribe of Manasseh

**v. 29:** "These were the descendants of Manasseh: The Machirite clan from Machir, the father of Gilead, and the Gileadite clan from Gilead."

- **Ellicott** notes that in 1 Chronicles 7:14, and in the Septuagint of Genesis 46:20, Machir's mother was an Aramitess. This may explain the name "Gilead," which was the borderland between Syria and Canaan, where Laban overtook Jacob (Genesis 31:25). (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/numbers-26.html)
- **Keil & Delitzsch** state that eight families descended from Manasseh: one from Machir, one from Machir's son Gilead, and six from the six sons of Gilead. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)

**vv. 30–32:** The six clans from Gilead's sons: Iezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher.

- **Keil & Delitzsch** note that Iezer (v. 30) is called Abiezer in Joshua 17:2. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)

**v. 33:** "Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons but only daughters. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah."

- **Keil & Delitzsch** explain that Zelophehad is mentioned specifically here because the fact that he had no sons but only daughters gives rise to the legal regulations in Numbers 27 and 36. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)
- **Benson** remarks: "It is remarkable that in so many heads of families there was only one to whom no sons were born. To what other cause can this be ascribed but to a peculiar providence, whereby many more males than females were born, for the strength and increase of the Jewish nation?" (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/numbers-26.html)
- **The Expositor's Bible Commentary** (via Bible Odyssey) notes that this case sets a precedent for daughters' inheritance in ancient Israel, though it disrupts the social order stipulating retention of land among men. The decision "marks the beginning of another conception — that of the personal development of women." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/teb/numbers-26.html)
- **Bible Odyssey** (modern scholarship) notes that the daughters did not receive the land Moses promised them until after the crossing of the Jordan (Joshua 17:3–4), and that Numbers 36 later required them to marry within their tribe to prevent land transfer. The story "demonstrates that Israelite daughters could inherit property — even if only to hold it in trust to pass on to their sons." (https://www.bibleodyssey.org/articles/zelophehads-daughters/)

**v. 34:** "These were the clans of Manasseh, and their registration numbered 52,700."

- **Enduring Word**: Manasseh experienced the largest increase of any tribe — from 32,200 to 52,700, a gain of 20,500 (64%). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)
- **Wesley** notes that this fulfills the prophecy of Genesis 49:22 concerning Joseph's posterity. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/numbers-26.html)
- **Benson** likewise connects it to the Genesis 49:22 promise. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/numbers-26.html)
- **Gill** exclaims: "the increase was 20,500, a large increase indeed!" (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)

---

### vv. 35–37 — The Tribe of Ephraim

**v. 35:** "These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: The Shuthelahite clan from Shuthelah, the Becherite clan from Becher, and the Tahanite clan from Tahan."

- **Keil & Delitzsch** note there were four families from Ephraim: three from his sons and one from his grandson (Eran, v. 36). (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)
- **Gill** records only three families, plus the Eranite branch from Shuthelah. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)

**v. 36:** "And the descendants of Shuthelah were the Eranite clan from Eran."

- **Keil & Delitzsch** observe that several links of Shuthelah's descendants are given in 1 Chronicles 7:20. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)

**v. 37:** "These were the clans of Ephraim, and their registration numbered 32,500."

- **Ellicott** records that this shows a decrease of 8,000 from the first census. He notes the irony: Jacob foretold Ephraim would be greater than Manasseh (Genesis 48:19), and at the first census Ephraim was indeed larger (40,500 vs. 32,200) and was made a standard-bearer. But now Manasseh exceeded Ephraim by 20,200 — "and yet, in the face of the great increase of Manasseh and the diminution of Ephraim, Moses renewed and confirmed the prediction of Jacob as to the ultimate superiority of Ephraim" (Deuteronomy 33:17: "the ten thousands of Ephraim"). (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/numbers-26.html)
- **Benson** similarly observes that Ephraim "though in future times a tribe flourishing much more than its brother-tribe Manasseh … was now, for some cause, upon the declension." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/numbers-26.html)
- **Enduring Word** notes the 20% decrease. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)

---

### vv. 38–41 — The Tribe of Benjamin

**v. 38:** "These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans: The Belaite clan from Bela, the Ashbelite clan from Ashbel, the Ahiramite clan from Ahiram…"

- **Wesley** observes that Benjamin originally had ten sons (Genesis 46:21), but only five are listed here — "the rest probably, together with their families, being extinct." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/numbers-26.html)
- **Benson** concurs: "Half of these, it seems, had no children, or their families were become extinct." He adds that in compensation, two grandsons through Bela — Ard and Naaman — became heads of large families. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/numbers-26.html)
- **Gill** notes that five sons are omitted, "perhaps because they died without issue." He observes the name variations: Ehi becomes Ahiram, and Huppim and Muppim become Shupham and Hupham. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)
- **Keil & Delitzsch**: "The children of Benjamin formed seven families, five of whom were founded by his sons, and two by grandsons." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)

**v. 40:** "And the descendants of Bela from Ard and Naaman were the Ardite clan from Ard and the Naamite clan from Naaman."

- These are the two grandson-founded clans that supplement the five son-founded clans, bringing Benjamin's total to seven.

**v. 41:** "These were the clans of Benjamin, and their registration numbered 45,600."

- **Enduring Word**: Benjamin increased from 35,400 to 45,600 — a gain of 10,200 (29%). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)
- **Gill**: "here was an increase of 10,200." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)

---

### vv. 42–43 — The Tribe of Dan

**v. 42:** "These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: The Shuhamite clan from Shuham. These were the clans of Dan."

- **Keil & Delitzsch**: Dan had only one son, called Shuham here but Hushim in Genesis 46:23. Yet this single family "no doubt branched out into several smaller families, which are not named here, simply because this list contains only the leading families into which the tribes were divided." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)
- **Gill** explains the plural "sons" (where there was only one son) as referring to Dan's posterity. The name Shuham appears as Hushim in Genesis 46:23 by transposition. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)
- **Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary** suggests: "If Dan had other children, it is likely they assimilated with the family of Shusham." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/numbers-26.html)

**v. 43:** "All of them were Shuhamite clans, and their registration numbered 64,400."

- **Wesley** draws a striking contrast: All 64,400 came from one son and one family, whereas Benjamin, with ten sons and five families, numbered only 45,600 — "to shew that the increase of families depends singly upon God's blessing and good pleasure." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/numbers-26.html)
- **Enduring Word**: Dan increased from 62,700 to 64,400 — a modest gain of 1,700 (3%). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)
- **Gill**: "yet, though but one, consisted of 64,400 men; there was an increase of 1700 in this tribe." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)
- **Matthew Henry** (via StudyLight.org) adds: "Of Dan but one, for Dan had but one son, and yet that tribe was the most numerous of all except Judah … Its beginning was small, but its latter end greatly increased." (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/numbers/26-23.html)

---

## Denominational Distinctives

This passage is largely genealogical and numerical, so denominational differences are minimal. However, some distinct emphases appear:

- **Wesleyan/Methodist (Wesley, Benson):** Both stress the *providential* hand of God behind the numbers — the increase of tribes is "according to the promise" (Genesis 49:22) and depends "singly upon God's blessing and good pleasure." This reflects the Wesleyan emphasis on God's active governance in history. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/numbers-26.html; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/numbers-26.html)

- **Reformed/Calvinistic (Gill):** Gill sees the tribal order as reflecting God's sovereign arrangement — Issachar and Zebulun are "under the standard" of Judah, a type of Christ. The variations in increase and decrease are presented matter-of-factly as God's sovereign determination. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/numbers-26.html)

- **Pentecostal/Charismatic (Enduring Word / David Guzik):** Guzik emphasizes the *spiritual condition* behind the population shifts — tribes that were faithful were blessed with increase, while unfaithfulness (e.g., Simeon's 63% loss) brought judgment. He frames the whole census as revealing "the spiritual condition of Israel through striking shifts in tribal populations." (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-26/)

- **Lutheran (Keil & Delitzsch):** The emphasis is on careful philological and historical precision — explaining name variations through Hebrew and Arabic etymology, treating the census as a sober historical document that prepares for both war and inheritance, without heavy devotional overlay. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/numbers-26.html)

- **Anglican (Ellicott):** Ellicott combines historical-grammatical precision with theological reflection, noting the irony of Ephraim's decline despite Jacob's prophecy, and observing how Moses reaffirmed that prophecy even against present numbers — a nuanced reading of providence. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/numbers-26.html)

---

## Modern Scholarship / Other Views

- **Bible Odyssey** (modern scholarship on Zelophehad's daughters, v. 33): The story "provides fodder for various discussions in the history of interpretation including those centered around female cooperation, patriarchal limitations, and divine justice." The daughters' inheritance was constrained — they had to marry within their tribe (Num. 36) — so the breakthrough, while real, was limited. (https://www.bibleodyssey.org/articles/zelophehads-daughters/)

- **The Expositor's Bible Commentary** (late 19th c. but often cited in modern study): Interprets the daughters' case as advancing "the personal development of women," giving them "a new position of responsibility as well as privilege." It even draws a modern application about inheritance laws under "modern social conditions." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/teb/numbers-26.html)

---

*Note: Catholic (newadvent.org, catholic.com) and Orthodox (oca.org) sources, as well as netbible.org notes, did not appear with specific commentary on this passage in the searches obtained.*
